summary: Every clip above 300k in this campaign locks one complete joke as a static text block visible from frame one — the punchline is absorbed in under two seconds, no reading required across cuts. The winning meme structure is a sharply specific, relatable premise (Lucia contradiction, Jason devotion, platform-envy) written in casual internet sentence case with 1-2 trailing emojis and zero lore dependency. Trending Shorts data confirms the broader GTA 6 space rewards emotional contrast and couple-dynamics content at massive scale (Jason & Lucia close-up thumbnails, 'good ending' arcs), but those clips run 49-58s with heavy editing — our 12s silent format must compete by landing the entire emotional hit in the hook text alone. moments_to_pick: Lucia doing something wholesome, domestic, or innocent that directly contradicts her criminal record — the contradiction IS the joke, requires zero lore
Jason visibly suffering, waiting, or sacrificing comfort entirely for Lucia's benefit — framed as helpless devotion, one sentence, no explanation needed
Jason & Lucia couple dynamic where Lucia is clearly in charge and Jason is lovesick and compliant — played for warmth and absurdity simultaneously
Platform-envy pain: PC players watching GTA 6 run on PS5 at launch — Vice City footage as backdrop, the suffering is the universal hook
Fan-loyalty sacrifice: someone doing an absurdly specific thing to prepare for Lucia's release or GTA 6's launch — the specificity makes it viral (see rank 3: '5am, drill, house ready')
Vice City skyline or trailer-iconic location used as backdrop for a one-sentence '13-year wait' or generational grief confession — legible to anyone who has heard of GTA

title_formula: State the meme premise in 7-11 words exactly as someone would type it in a comment — conversational, no forced grammar, no 'When' or 'POV' opener. caption_formula: One sentence (max 18 words) that restates the meme idea in different wording from the on-screen text — never copy it verbatim, adds a small emotional kicker the text didn't. avoid: Changing the on-screen text between shots — ranks 1, 2, 4 all hold one static block across every beat; this is the dominant proven pattern and must not be broken until the escalating experiment has ru
ALL CAPS text — every high-performing campaign clip uses sentence case; caps reads aggressive, not relatable, in this meme register
More than 2 emojis inside the on-screen text block — top clips use exactly 1-2 at the tail end only; front-loaded or clustered emojis do not appear in any top performer
Premises that require deep GTA 6 lore — the top clips are legible to anyone who has seen Lucia's face once; lore-heavy jokes narrow the audience before the hook lands
Soft setups with no absurdist spike or contradiction — warmth without a sharp contrast consistently underperforms; the joke needs a gap between expectation and reality
Voiceover, dialogue, music other than Tokyo Girl — campaign rule, zero exceptions
